original_question: Let C be a non-circular closed convex planar curve. Prove that there exists a constant V_C > 0, depending only on C, such that for every compact embedded constant-mean-curvature disk Sigma spanning C with volume V > 0, the following threshold behavior holds: if V <= V_C then Sigma lies on one side of the boundary plane P; if V = V_C then Sigma is tangent to P at the points of minimum curvature of C; and if V > V_C then Sigma has points on both sides of P.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.7 (4*), the volume-threshold problem for compact embedded cmc disks spanning a non-circular closed convex planar curve. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended target almost word-for-word: the boundary curve is non-circular, closed, convex, and planar; the surface is a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature disk spanning that curve; the unknown is a threshold constant V_C depending only on C; and the three regimes V≤V_C, V=V_C, and V>V_C are exactly the ones stated in the paper, including tangency to the boundary plane at minimum-curvature points when V=V_C. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
missing_details: The ambient space should be stated explicitly: the paper works in Euclidean three-space R^3. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

The symbol P must be defined as the plane containing the planar curve C; in the paper this notation is fixed in the preliminary section. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

To match the paper precisely, Σ should be described as a compact embedded cmc disk in R^3 with boundary C (or equivalently, spanning C in the paper's sense). ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

Because the statement refers to points of minimum curvature of C, some smoothness of C is implicit; the paper is written in the differential-geometric setting where curvature of the boundary curve is meaningful. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

The phrases "lies in one side of P" and "has points in both sides of P" should be understood relative to the two half-spaces determined by P. This is implicit in the surrounding discussion of planar boundary problems. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

Your draft says "boundary plane P" without defining it; the paper simply uses P for the plane containing C. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

The paper poses this as an open problem to prove, not as a theorem already established. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

If one wants the question to be completely stand-alone, the notion of "volume V>0" should be tied to the fixed-volume Plateau setting discussed immediately before Problem 3.7; the paper itself leaves that notion implicit. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
refined_question: Let C⊂R^3 be a smooth closed convex planar curve that is not a round circle, and let P be the plane containing C. Does there exist a constant V_C>0, depending only on C, such that every compact embedded constant-mean-curvature topological disk Σ⊂R^3 with boundary C and prescribed volume V>0 satisfies the following trichotomy: (i) if V≤V_C, then Σ is contained in one of the two closed half-spaces determined by P; (ii) if V=V_C, then Σ is tangent to P at the points of C where the curvature of C is minimal; and (iii) if V>V_C, then Σ meets both open half-spaces determined by P? ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
justification: This draft is clearly not aiming at the introductory circle conjectures from Section 1; it matches the official formulation of Section 3, Problem 3.7. The nearby context explains why this particular threshold question is asked: for sufficiently small prescribed volume, convex planar boundary forces a cmc surface to be a graph, while a large-volume result of Ros and Rosenberg is recalled from Section 2. The notation P for the plane containing C is fixed in the preliminaries, so adding that definition is the main step needed to make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
